display.purpose: The name in the first viewport, set like the wordmark: "Lupi" 700, "OS" 400, -0.04em, frost. The download page title uses it up to 5rem.

headline.purpose: Section heads on top of each species account (up to 3.4rem, -0.035em); up to 2.75rem beside commands on the download page.

title.purpose: Ruled-grid entry heads and switch option names (1.2rem), key specimen names (1.45rem), Habitat column heads (1.45rem).

name-latin.purpose: Set in italic: the binomial (1.25rem, ice), neighbour species names (1.15rem), plate credits (0.92rem).

body.purpose: Running text at 1.0625rem. Section intros 1.125rem at 54ch, ledes 46ch (download page 56ch), asides 66ch.

body-small.purpose: Tables, legends, side notes, asides, colophon.

label.purpose: Bold sentence case (Arimo 700, 0.85-0.9rem): table heads, command labels, phone row labels, the trait column. The status tag is the one uppercase label.

code.purpose: Inline commands in frost; command names in ruled grids at 1.1rem in ice; command plates at 0.9rem.

motion.name: ease
motion.purpose: The only easing: soft exponential out, for every transition and the load moment.

motion.name: rule-in
motion.value: clip-path inset(0 100% 0 0) to inset(0) over 1.8s, 0.1s delay
motion.purpose: The ridge draws left to right on load.

motion.name: draw
motion.value: clip-path inset(0 0 0 100%) to inset(0) over 1.1s, 0.25s delay
motion.purpose: The plate's leader lines reveal on load.

motion.name: land
motion.value: opacity 0 and scale(0.6) to rest over 0.6s, 80ms stagger from 0.9s
motion.purpose: Field marks land in sequence after the lines draw (the Den's when it comes into view).

motion.name: rule
motion.value: scaleX(0) to 1 from the left, 1.1s; rows by background-size, 0.8s, 70ms stagger capped at 7; entry rules 0.9s, 90ms stagger
motion.purpose: Each account rules its lines in once it scrolls into view (.motion + .drawn). Only lines and marks start hidden, never text.

motion.name: leader
motion.purpose: The key's dotted leader runs out to its answer on hover or focus.

motion.name: page
motion.purpose: Pages crossfade (the masthead stays put); in-page links scroll smoothly.

motion.name: reduced
motion.value: prefers-reduced-motion: reduce: no .motion, no animation, no smooth scroll, no view transition
motion.purpose: Colour transitions stay, because they carry state.

narrative.overview:
LupiOS is shown as a species in a field guide printed for night use: total navy plates, ice-blue hairlines, numbered leader-line callouts on real photographs (VM screenshots), names in the logo's own Helvetica letter shapes (Arimo) with italic Latin, and bold labels. It continues the OS's own night identity (ice-blue wolf mark on deep navy, mountain ridges, the palette in `art/generate.mjs`), so the website, wallpapers, installer and link preview read as one brand.

Hierarchy comes from type and ink, never from boxes or light. Content is set as "species accounts": the heading and its intro on top, the account across the full width below, each account opened by one hairline rule; side notes sit beside the table, plate or key they explain. Comparisons are ruled tables, explanations are ruled heading-and-text grids, and evidence is a plate with numbered marks. Density is that of a reference book: generous section breaks, tight ruled rows inside.

The world is dark only by design: the brand is night. The field-guide pages (the home page and the download page, framed by `src/layouts/GuideLayout.astro`) set `color-scheme: dark` on their root and offer no light variant. The docs pages stay Starlight (lupios.css), with a light theme as well, but follow this world's structure: in the dark theme one night plate (header and sidebar included) set apart by hairlines, frost headings, ice links, the ochre focus ring, commands as frost ink rather than boxes, the current page marked by bold ice and a hairline instead of a filled box; the light theme keeps that structure in deep blue on white. They share the typeface (Arimo, JetBrains Mono for commands) and the page-to-page crossfade, so moving between them feels like one site.
keyCharacteristics: Navy plate background, edge to edge, with ice hairlines as the only structure.
Arimo throughout (the Helvetica letter shapes of the logo): bold display set like the wordmark, regular body, italic for names. JetBrains Mono for commands.
One ochre, reserved for what the reader is pointed at.
Real screenshots as plates, annotated with numbered circular field marks and short ticks.
Flat: no cards, no glow, no gradients.
Motion is ink being drawn: the first viewport draws itself on load, and each account rules its lines in as it comes into view.

rules.name: The Pointed-At Rule
rules.body: Ochre marks only what the reader is being pointed at: a status, a focus, a chosen state, the answer to the key, LupiOS among its neighbours. Never decoration, never a second brand colour, never more than one pointed-at thing per view in normal reading.

rules.name: The Ink-Not-Box Rule
rules.body: Emphasis is done by moving text up the ink ladder (dim, ink, frost, ice, ochre), not by putting it in a filled container.

rules.name: The Wordmark Rule
rules.body: Type follows the logo: one neo-grotesque (Arimo) for everything but code, headings tight (-0.015 to -0.04em) like the wordmark, and the name in the first viewport set exactly as the logo is (bold "Lupi", regular "OS"). No second display family.

rules.name: The One Stamp Rule
rules.body: Capitals appear once per page: the ochre status tag (700, 0.78rem, 0.08em). Every other label is bold sentence case.

rules.name: The Italic Is a Name Rule
rules.body: Italic is reserved for names (species, Latin) and photo credits.

rules.name: The Flat Plate Rule
rules.body: Surfaces are the night plate itself. A thing is set apart by a hairline, never by a fill or a glow.

dos: Do keep every page of this world on the night plate (night) edge to edge, dark only.
Do structure with hairlines (hairline between sections and rows, hairline-strong above grid entries and around inset plates).
Do set content as accounts: the heading and intro on top, the account across the full width, side notes beside what they explain.
Do prove features with real screenshots as plates, annotated with numbered circular field marks, a legend and a provenance credit.
Do hold ochre for the pointed-at thing: status, focus ring, chosen state, key answer, LupiOS's own row.
Do use Arimo for everything but code, with tight headings and LupiOS set like the wordmark; italic only for names and Latin.
Do make comparison tables collapse to labelled blocks per row below 52rem.
donts: Don't wrap content in cards: no filled or shadowed boxes around text groups. Bordered plates around photographs and the terminal transcript are the world's own material and stay.
Don't add glow, gradients or a gradient hero over an icon-card grid.
Don't introduce a second warm accent or use ochre decoratively.
Don't bring back a second display family, or uppercase labels beyond the one status tag.
Don't leave a column empty for symmetry: an account's side column holds real notes or nothing.
Don't add motion that isn't a line being drawn or a mark landing (no fade-and-rise sections, no parallax); state changes only ease colour.
Don't invent screenshots, users, numbers or testimonials for plates or marks.
